## Overview

This Adapter Validation Suite (AVS) instantiates the [UIAO_121 Adapter Conformance Test Plan](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/adapter-conformance-test-plan-template.md) for the `opm-azure-apim` adapter. It defines the Tier-1 contract-conformance criteria, the controls under validation, and the integration test plan that govern the adapter across its lifecycle.

## Validation status

**Reserved slot — not yet implemented.** `opm-azure-apim` is `status: reserved` / `phase: phase-planning` in canon. No adapter code exists yet. The Tier-1 criteria below define the conformance gate the adapter **must** clear at activation; they are a forward-looking plan, not a current result.

## Scope

Target surfaces / subsystems: `oauth2-token-validation`, `api-rate-limiting`, `mtls-termination`, `payload-transformation`, `developer-portal`, `cross-agency-api-routing`

**Validation artifacts:** `apim-policy-manifest.json`, `apim-traffic-audit.json`, `apim-developer-portal-inventory.json`

The suite validates that, for each target surface, the adapter normalizes vendor data into canonical claims, emits deterministic provenance, and produces KSI-anchored evidence — without mutating any source system (`ssot-mutation: never`).

## Controls under validation

The control roles below are mirrored from the adapter's companion [Adapter Technical Specification](../../../adapter-specs/opm-azure-apim/opm-azure-apim.html); the validation suite verifies that the adapter produces the evidence each role asserts.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls this adapter supports: `AC-4`, `AC-17`, `AU-2`, `AU-12`, `IA-2`, `IA-8`, `SC-7`, `SC-8`, `SC-13`, `SC-23`, `CA-9`

| Control | Role | Adapter capability |
|---|---|---|
| **AC-4** Information Flow Enforcement | Primary | APIM policy enforces information flow at the federally-mandated gateway boundary. |
| **AC-17** Remote Access | Primary | Cross-agency API routing is the canonical remote-access surface for federal-HRIT consumers. |
| **AU-2** Event Logging | Primary | Every API call traversing the gateway is logged with the canonical request envelope. |
| **AU-12** Audit Record Generation | Supporting | Audit records carry the canonical provenance envelope per ADR-006. |
| **IA-2** Identification and Authentication | Primary | OAuth 2.0 token validation at gateway ingress is the canonical authentication path for federal-HRIT API consumers. |
| **IA-8** Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users) | Supporting | Cross-agency consumers authenticate at the gateway boundary. |
| **SC-7** Boundary Protection | Primary | APIM is the federally-mandated boundary enforcement point for federal-HRIT traffic. |
| **SC-8** Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | Primary | mTLS termination at the gateway is the canonical evidence of TLS-protected transit. |
| **SC-13** Cryptographic Protection | Supporting | Validation uses FIPS-validated cryptographic libraries. |
| **SC-23** Session Authenticity | Supporting | mTLS-anchored session identity flows through the gateway as canonical headers. |
| **CA-9** Internal System Connections | Primary | The gateway is the canonical interconnection point between consuming-agency systems and the Core HCM platform. |

## Notes from canon

Closes the HRIT IAM gap for the centralized OPM-hosted API gateway mandated by Solicitation 24322626R0007 Amd 4 Appendix B pp. 82, 84. Gateway is operated by OPM; the contractor configures APIs through it but does not own the gateway. The "Core-HCM API boundary" is enforced at this surface — the contractor's responsibility ends at APIM ingress. Adapter activation requires an OPM-issued service principal scoped to the federal-HRIT APIM instance. Tier-1 conformance: pending — likely requires Microsoft-attested test fixtures plus per-tenant sandbox capture. Activation requires a per-adapter ADR modeled on ADR-035.
